protocol.purpose: Frozen-policy complete-task development benchmark; no learning or hardware
protocol.online_information: Both MPC variants use current full simulator state and frozen policy history; future disturbance is not provided. Policy rollout has privileged exact nominal physics; no hardware-realism claim.

original_execution_receipt.first_run: six cases completed; stopped before policy-rollout case when unsupported mj_copyData was accessed
original_execution_receipt.continuation: only three previously unexecuted policy-rollout cases; all saved before final stdout ndarray serialization failure

timestamp_hold_correction.replacement_selection: Only explicitly supplied method/condition replacements; all other original cases retained

totals.settling_scope: Derived for the nine completed task cases only; locomotion validation and startup/debug overhead are separate

all_attempt_totals_including_superseded.scope: All original and replacement completed task attempts, including superseded cases; other startup/debug and locomotion work separate

setup_and_failure_accounting.clone_failure_count_source: Saved clone exception and original runner reset-before-planner order; not a finalized process counter

weight_identity_evidence.scope: File hashes and frozen execution provenance; no additional policy inference or weight mutation performed by analysis

process_status_note: Original six cases saved before clone API exception; three original unexecuted cases continued separately; final stdout serialization exception occurred after saving continuation results. Timestamp-hold replacements, if supplied, are separate additional executions. Do not claim original processes had clean exit 0.
interpretation_limits: All feedback weights are frozen; differences are command planning and prediction differences, not new learned capability.
Policy rollout uses privileged exact nominal simulator dynamics and full policy history. Zero nonpush error is same-simulator consistency, not generalization or real-robot accuracy.
Kinematic collision scoring uses an approximate heading-aware rectangle; policy-rollout scoring uses full simulated contact. Outcome differences are not isolated solely to dynamics prediction.
Future force is absent from planning. A push macro is a deliberate unpredicted intervention; later forecasts restart from the actual perturbed state/history.
Physical simulation is paused while planning. Missed 0.2s computation periods are not inserted as actuation delay; successful simulated tasks are not real-time deployment validation.
Torque-squared integral and absolute mechanical work are distinct physical proxies, not measured electrical energy.
Three deterministic conditions are development evidence, not success-rate probability, robustness proof, or hardware transfer.
First-run process CPU/total wall counters were not finalized after its exception; completed per-case wall times remain available. Do not invent a total process CPU time.
